title: Alien Arithmetic: prime-letter notation, the prime shift map, odd perfect numbers and Descartes numbers
description: Research notes, code, data and Lean 4 proofs (no Mathlib) built around writing integers as vectors of prime exponents ('alien' notation). Contents: (1) the prime shift map sigma (OEIS A003961): structural theorems, density of sigma(n+1) > sigma(n), equidistribution mod q, shift twins up to 10^11, aliquot-type dynamics; (2) odd perfect numbers: Euler's and Touchard's theorems in core Lean and a verified forcing-chain engine proving in Lean that an odd perfect number has at least 7 distinct prime factors (re-proofs of known results); (3) Descartes (spoof odd perfect) numbers n*x with sigma(n)(x+1) = 2nx: Lean proofs that n is a perfect square 2n - sigma(n) divides n and sigma(n)/n >= 9/5, and an exhaustive search showing that any Descartes number other than Descartes' 1638 example has n > 10^26 (previous published bound 10^12, Toth 2021).
